title: fix(analyze): first class citizen snippets

## Summary

Part of https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/8590
Closes https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/11841

I used a coding agent to help myself. I carefully planned the feature, then surgically made the smallest changes, one at the time.

Up until now, host document suppressions couldn't suppress signals emitted by guest languages. To fix this, the analyser must know about them. 

This PR creates the concept of `SnippetAnalyzer` and `EmbeddedSignalInspect`. The `Analyzer` can now accept multiple `SnippetAnalyzer`, and for each instance we have the inspector that passes the suppressions recorded for each line.

- Created a new `SnippetAnalyzer` trait. This is implemented by guest languages. Internally, guest structs need to know about their CST, rules, etc. They are minimal analysers; however, their signals are sent to the host analyser
- `EmbeddedSignalInspector` is the type that inspects and collects the signals emitted by the guest analysers
- Moved the logic for "suppress a signal" to `Suppressions`. This logic isn't kept inside `flush_matches`, so we can use it inside guest languages too
- Added a `run_snippet` method, which analyses a snippet. It passes an inspector, so that its signals are matched against the suppressions collected by the host analyser. 
- Added the proper snippet analysers in the relevant languages 
- The workspace server now **doesn't** loop over snippets. Instead, it passes snippets to the underlying function, and the analyser handles them.
